_meta.survival_funding_config_note: Atlas Survival Phase 2B (supabase/migrations/20260924120000_survival_funding_phase2b.sql). APPLIED to production 2026-09-24 (ledger name survival_funding_phase2b) and observed live at capture time; the row above is as-observed, not inferred from migration text. CURRENT TRUTH for the owner-declared operating capital: a SERVER-ONLY singleton holding exactly one row (id = 1, enforced by a CHECK), seeded NULL, and NULL means UNDECLARED rather than zero. RLS enabled with ZERO policies; anon and authenticated hold no grant at all; service_role holds SELECT and nothing else, so no role anywhere has INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE — which is what makes the SECURITY DEFINER setter survival_set_declared_operating_capital the only writer that can exist, and why no owner-check trigger was needed. It has no sequences: `id integer primary key` has no default and no identity. The `service_role: true` boolean records REACHABILITY only and cannot express privilege breadth — production grants SELECT and nothing more. It is deliberately NOT on platform_config, whose authenticated_read_platform_config policy has qual `true` and would have published this value to every authenticated user.
_meta.survival_funding_events_note: Atlas Survival Phase 2B (supabase/migrations/20260924120000_survival_funding_phase2b.sql). APPLIED to production 2026-09-24 and observed live at capture time. APPEND-ONLY AUDIT EVIDENCE for changes to the declaration — never a source of current truth, which is survival_funding_config; nothing reads this table to answer what is declared now. Zero rows at capture time (no synthetic evidence was inserted to prove it). RLS enabled with ZERO policies; anon and authenticated hold no grant at all; service_role holds SELECT and nothing else. No role holds INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE, and the identity sequence survival_funding_events_event_seq_seq is revoked from every role, so the SECURITY DEFINER setter is the only writer. Two triggers enforce append-only structurally: BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE per row and BEFORE TRUNCATE per statement, both raising 42501.
_meta.survival_state_events_note: Atlas Survival Phase 2A (supabase/migrations/20260923120000_survival_state_events.sql). APPLIED to production 2026-09-24 and observed live at capture time; its row above is as-observed, not inferred from migration text. RLS is enabled with zero client policies, anon and authenticated hold no table grants at all, and service_role's reach is SELECT on the table plus EXECUTE on the reviewed SECURITY DEFINER recorder RPC survival_record_observation. That function is the ONLY writer: no role holds INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE, and the identity sequence is revoked from every role. The `service_role: true` boolean records REACHABILITY only and cannot express privilege breadth — production grants SELECT and EXECUTE and nothing else. The recorder remains DORMANT in Phase 2A: no scheduler or runtime path calls it, so the table is empty. Generated type files have not been reconciled to production.
_meta.regenerate: Introspect pg_class.relrowsecurity, pg_policies and information_schema.role_table_grants for schema 'public' and rewrite this file. lib/qa/schema-security-invariant.test.ts defines the exact contract each entry must satisfy.

classes.SERVER_ONLY: Service-role only. anon and authenticated hold NO grants at all. RLS must be enabled.
classes.TENANT_RLS: Reached by user-bound clients under an owner-rooted policy. Default Supabase grants remain and are inert because RLS gates every row. RLS must be enabled and at least one policy must exist.
classes.INTERNAL_DENY_ALL: RLS enabled with zero policies: default-deny for anon and authenticated. Grants remain but reach nothing. Safe; revoking them too would be belt-and-braces.
classes.INTENTIONALLY_PUBLIC: Deliberately reachable without a session. Requires an explicit reviewed entry and may hold SELECT only, never DML. NONE exist today — the class is declared so a future one is a deliberate, reviewed act rather than a silent default.

limitations: This is a point-in-time capture. A change made directly in the Supabase dashboard after capture is not detected until the file is regenerated.
It records grants and RLS state, not policy semantics: a policy that is present but wrongly written is out of scope here and is covered by the route-level isolation suites.
The paired migration-text rule in the invariant is forward-looking only; it governs tables created from now on.
The registry is a live-catalog snapshot, so a migration-created table that is not live is absent by construction; _meta.created_not_live records those and the invariant requires each to declare RLS.

out_of_band_rls.meaning: Empty since Phase 9Z. It previously held dream_issues, whose RLS existed in production but was declared in no migration. Closure audit #4 showed that was not an isolated case and not merely documentation debt: a database rebuilt from repo SQL created dream_issues, cost_rates and morning_briefings with RLS OFF and anon DML live. supabase/migrations/20260910090000_declarative_rls_parity.sql declares all three, so the exception has no remaining subject.
out_of_band_rls.rule: An entry here excuses a table from the migration-text rule. It must still be RLS-enabled in effective state, and it should be treated as temporary: an exception that outlives its cause is a hole with a comment next to it.

created_not_live.meaning: Created by a migration but absent from the production catalog at capture time — never applied there, or dropped out-of-band. They are NOT a fresh-deploy hazard: each declares RLS in its own migration, so a rebuild creates them protected. Listed so their absence from the table map is a recorded fact rather than a silent gap, and so the fail-closed rule can distinguish them from a genuinely new unprotected table.
created_not_live.requirement: Every entry must have RLS declared in the migration corpus.
created_not_live.classes_note: The migration security gate needs a class for every table a migration touches. These entries are not live, so they cannot be introspected. Their creating migrations make them server-only (RLS enabled, client grants revoked), so SERVER_ONLY is their intended class.
created_not_live.run_autonomy_decisions_note: Phase 3B1A (20260925120000_autonomy_trace_decisions.sql). NOT YET APPLIED to production — this branch is local and the phase explicitly forbids applying it, so the row cannot be introspected and its class is declared from the migration the same way the other entries are. The migration creates it with RLS enabled, ZERO policies, every client grant revoked, and SELECT granted to service_role alone; the only write path is the SECURITY DEFINER RPC record_run_autonomy_decision, which holds no INSERT grant for any role. SERVER_ONLY is therefore its intended and only correct class. When the migration is eventually applied, this entry should be replaced by an introspected row in `tables`, in the same way platform_credential_events was.

_meta.post_migration: 20260909120000_workflow_stories_rls.sql (Phase 9Y) and 20260910090000_declarative_rls_parity.sql (Phase 9Z). Every row reflects effective production state, which those two migrations now also declare; and 20260910120000_cost_ledger_rls_isolation.sql (Phase 9AB), which moves cost_events and infra_costs from TENANT_RLS to SERVER_ONLY: their `project_id IS NULL OR …` policies on role public are dropped and anon/authenticated grants revoked.
_meta.views: Phase 9AA. Public VIEWS, classified like tables. A view runs as its owner unless it is security_invoker, so base-table RLS does not protect it; the migration security gate fails any client-reachable public view without security_invoker and any public view absent from this map. `live` records whether it exists in production.
_meta.atlas_code_broker_note: Phase 1C1A trusted broker identity (supabase/migrations/20260923150000_sdf1c1_trusted_broker_identity.sql). APPLIED to production 2026-09-24 (ledger name sdf1c1_trusted_broker_identity) and observed live at capture time; the rows above are as-observed, not inferred from migration text. Both tables: RLS enabled, zero policies, anon and authenticated hold no table grants, service_role holds SELECT only (no INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE for any role). The `service_role: true` boolean records REACHABILITY only. All mutation goes through five SECURITY DEFINER functions (atlas_code_broker_begin_enrollment, _complete_enrollment, _approve, _revoke, _accept_request) that only service_role may EXECUTE, guarded by BEFORE UPDATE triggers and BEFORE DELETE/TRUNCATE reject triggers. Both tables were empty at apply time. Identity and enrollment only: the dormant broker_token_* seam on atlas_code_work_runs is untouched, and no claim, heartbeat, evidence or transition path references these tables. Generated type file synced in the same PR.
_meta.autonomy_license_phase2c_note: Atlas Autonomy Licensing Phase 2C (supabase/migrations/20260924180000_autonomy_license_phase2c.sql). APPLIED to production on 2026-09-25 (ledger name autonomy_license_phase2c, Supabase ledger version 20260925102918) and observed live at capture time; the row above is as-observed, not inferred from migration text. The table exists and held ZERO rows at evidence capture — no licence has been issued, and nothing in this note should be read as one having been. SERVER_ONLY: RLS enabled with ZERO policies, anon and authenticated hold no grant at all, and service_role holds SELECT and nothing else, so no role anywhere has direct INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE. The identity sequence atlas_autonomy_license_events_event_seq_seq is revoked from every role, and two triggers enforce append-only structurally (BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE per row, BEFORE TRUNCATE per statement, both raising 42501), which makes the SECURITY DEFINER function autonomy_license_append the single reviewed write path that can exist. That writer has an EMPTY search_path, is executable only by postgres and service_role (not PUBLIC, anon or authenticated), and carries p_expected_generation — the caller's observed lineage generation, compared against the locked truth before any insert and refused with SQLSTATE 40001 when stale. The previous 17-parameter writer signature is absent, leaving exactly one overload. The `service_role: true` boolean records REACHABILITY only and cannot express privilege breadth — production grants SELECT and nothing more. Chapter 18 licence truth only: Phase 2C still has NO runtime execution consumer, and no executor, gate, provider, spend boundary or scheduler reads this table.
